title: 2026 Autumn Newsletter – Message by the Executive President and the Secretary General
content:
As an introduction to the Europa Nostra Newsletter issued on 23 October 2026

Dear members, partners and supporters of Europa Nostra,
Dear colleagues and friends,

Welcome to the Autumn edition of the Europa Nostra Newsletter! As you will read, the last  months have been marked by important advocacy action and impactful events held all over Europe, including numerous activities organised as part of our EU-funded European Heritage Hub project which are shared with you through dedicated newsletters.  

A protest gathering will be held on 29 October (09:30-11:30) at Schuman Square in Brussels to Stand up for AgoraEU. © Culture Action Europe

title: ANSCH Conference: Building bridges to protect cultural heritage amid conflict and climate challenges
content:
At the ANSCH (The Arab Network of Civil Society Organizations to Safeguard Cultural Heritage) Building Resilience Conference, supported by the Cultural Protection Fund of the British Council: “Building Resilience: Empowering Civil Society to Protect Heritage Amid Conflict and Climate Challenges,” held online on 19 October 2026, Europa Nostra Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović highlighted the vital role of civil society, local communities and international cooperation in safeguarding (endangered) cultural heritage.

Credit: Europa Nostra

During the panel “International Organisations and the Future of Heritage Protection,” she underscored four priorities: connecting organisations and networks, sharing knowledge and expertise, strengthening the voices of local civil society, and building lasting partnerships across the Mediterranean and beyond. She highlighted that Europa Nostra aspires to expand its work to benefit the entire area of “Mare Nostrum”.

Credit: Europa Nostra

title: Europa Nostra expresses deep concern over the proposed cuts to the AgoraEU programme
content:
Europa Nostra stands in solidarity with the European cultural and civil society community and expresses its deep concern over the proposed cuts to the AgoraEU programme in the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU’s negotiating box for the EU’s 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), published on 10 October 2026.

The proposal would reduce the AgoraEU programme’s budget from the European Commission’s proposed €8.6 billion to €6 billion in current prices — a decrease of around 30%. With the next European Council Summit starting tomorrow, EU leaders have an opportunity to reconsider this proposal and maintain the level of ambition needed to support Europe’s cultural and democratic life.

Image: Courtesy of Culture Action Europe

title: Hispania Nostra marks its 50th anniversary with its 45th Forum of Cultural Associations and Heritage Managers in Valencia
content:
Hispania Nostra, Europa Nostra’s country representation in Spain, held its 45th Forum, entitled “50 Years Committed to the Future of Cultural Heritage”, in Valencia  from 1 to 3 October 2026. Marking the 50th anniversary of Hispania Nostra, the Forum provided a meeting place for heritage professionals, associations and organisations to reflect on the evolution of heritage protection, the contribution of cultural associations and the future of cultural and natural heritage in Spain. Europa Nostra’s Advocacy and Partnerships Manager Vanessa Fraga Prol contributed to the Forum. 

Photo: Courtesy of Hispania Nostra

Organised annually, the Forum brings together professionals, members, associations and other individuals and organisations committed to the defence and protection of cultural and natural heritage. It offers a space to discuss a selected theme, share experiences and exchange views on current challenges and future priorities.

title: Europa Nostra Council calls for cultural heritage to be recognised as a cornerstone of a renewed vision for EU’s future
content:
The 2026 State of the European Union address (SOTEU) and preparations for the 70th anniversary of the Treaties of Rome in March 2027 were high on the agenda of Europa Nostra’s Council Meetings held on 8-10 October 2026 in Geneva, Switzerland. Discussions highlighted the need to place cultural heritage at the heart of a renewed European vision, strengthening democratic resilience and reconnecting citizens with the European project.

Photo credit: Europa Nostra

In the SOTEU delivered on 16 September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for a new vision for Europe: “The state of our Union is the strongest it has ever been. The state of our Union can also feel as precarious as it has ever been. These two statements may seem incompatible. But they are both true. And they reflect these exceptional times. This complex age of great possibilities and great perils which all countries are seeking to navigate. In this world, Europe has chosen to forge its own path. And a stronger, independent Europe is now emerging”. She also highlighted Europe’s core values, new partnerships and role in the world, looking ahead to the 2027 anniversary.

title: Europa Nostra strengthens ties with Swiss heritage organisations and partners during Council Meetings in Geneva
content:
Europa Nostra’s Council Meetings in Geneva, held from 8 to 10 October 2026, provided an opportunity to meet with Swiss Member and Associate Organisations, as well as other heritage associations and foundations based in the city. The exchanges offered a valuable opportunity to share experiences and explore how civil society can contribute to safeguarding Europe’s cultural heritage.

We were especially delighted to reconnect on this occasion with the Swiss Heritage Society, one of Europa Nostra’s founding organisations. In 1963, Europa Nostra was established through the initiative of heritage NGOs from seven European countries: Italy, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Switzerland, France, Germany and Ireland. This founding spirit of cross-border cooperation and peer-learning continues to underpin Europa Nostra’s mission today.

title: Europa Nostra members undertake enriching visits to (award-winning) cultural heritage sites in Geneva and Jussy
content:
As part of the Europa Nostra Council Meetings held in Geneva from 8 to 10 October 2026, Europa Nostra members undertook enriching visits to cultural heritage sites in Geneva, four of which received Europa Nostra Awards, namely the Société de Lecture, the Archaeological Site of Saint Pierre Cathedral, a Belle Époque Steamer and the Patek Philippe Museum, host of Philippe Stern’s Collection of Timekeepers.

Together, these visits offered a vivid illustration of the diversity of heritage recognised by the Europa Nostra Awards, spanning four award-winning initiatives across three categories between 2008 and 2020. The visits also demonstrated how the impact of the Awards extends far beyond the moment of recognition, continuing to inspire, engage and enrich Geneva’s cultural landscape today. They also highlighted the lasting sense of pride that receiving a Europa Nostra Award brings to the winning organisations and the people behind them, recognising their dedication and achievements while strengthening their commitment to safeguarding Europe’s shared cultural heritage.

title: (Re)Appointments of Europa Nostra Vice-Presidents and Treasurer in Geneva
content:
During its meetings held in Geneva on 8-10 October 2026, the Europa Nostra Council re-appointed Bertrand de Feydeau (France), Cristina Loglio (Italy) and Natalia Moussienko (Ukraine) as Vice-Presidents of Europa Nostra, for another term of 3 years. 

Photo credit: Europa Nostra

The Council also appointed Jacques de Saussure (Switzerland) as a new Vice-President of Europa Nostra. During his mandate, he will represent the voice of private owners of heritage monuments and sites; he will be Europa Nostra’s ambassador in Geneva, a European historic city with immense international outreach and global influence, and he will contribute to the development of Europa Nostra’s Mare Nostrum initiative.  

Members of the Council expressed highest esteem and deepest gratitude for the invaluable contribution made by two outgoing Vice-Presidents, Androulla Vassiliou (Cyprus) and Alexander zu Sayn-Wittgenstein-Sayn (Germany).

title: IN MEMORIAM: Sir Donald Insall CBE (1926-2026, United Kingdom)
content:
Europa Nostra has learned with sadness of the passing of our great friend, ally and advocate, Sir Donald Insall, on 10 October 2026, at the age of 100 years and eight months. Donald Insall was a pioneering conservationist, architect, planning consultant, author and teacher; he founded Donald Insall Associates in 1958, one of Britain’s leading conservation practices.

Photo source: Donald Insall Associates

He has been well known in our community since our foundation. Ours is a world demanding principled, inspired leadership. It has been cruelly and unfairly said that good designers design, but those who don’t, conserve. Sir Donald broke that prejudice by being a trailblazer in every respect.

title: Five winners from Italy honoured together in San Benedetto Po
content:
On 3 October, the Grand Prix 2026 in Conservation and Adaptive Reuse awarded to the Polirone Monastic Complex in San Benedetto Po was celebrated with a full day dedicated to cultural heritage, its preservation and its role in the life of local communities.

The long-term restoration of the thousand-year-old monastic complex addressed the damage caused by the 2012 earthquake, safeguarded its historic fabric and breathed new life into the site through renewed cultural and civic functions. Today, the complex once again stands at the heart of San Benedetto Po, serving as a vibrant centre for the town’s cultural and community life.

Entitled Polirone: Heritage of Europe (“Polirone: Patrimonio d’Europa”), the event brought together institutions, cultural and civic organisations, local stakeholders and citizens to celebrate a remarkable achievement made possible by their collective commitment to the protection, understanding and enhancement of the Polirone Monastic Complex.
